questions.sec: Coronary Territories, Dominance & Right Coronary Artery
questions.q: Which infarct territories are assigned to right coronary circulation on the source overview?
opts: Apical, high-lateral and anterior MI only
questions.exp: Right coronary circulation is linked to IWMI, PWMI and RVMI; left circulation is linked to AWMI, septal MI and LWMI. (Book p425)

questions.sec: Coronary Territories, Dominance & Right Coronary Artery
questions.q: Which chamber forms the anterior sternocostal surface of the heart in the source anatomy list?
questions.exp: Surface list: anterior sternocostal = RV; inferior diaphragmatic = RV+LV; posterior = LA. (Book p425)

questions.sec: Coronary Territories, Dominance & Right Coronary Artery
questions.q: A patient has a posterior descending artery arising from the RCA. Which dominance pattern and approximate frequency does the page give?
questions.exp: Dominance is based on the artery supplying posterior interventricular sulcus/PDA: RCA gives right dominance (85%); LCx gives left dominance (15%). (Book p425)

questions.sec: Coronary Territories, Dominance & Right Coronary Artery
questions.q: Which leads are listed for inferior-wall involvement in right coronary circulation?
questions.exp: Inferior leads are II, III, aVF; RV free-wall V3R/V4R/V5R and posterior V7/V8/V9 are not represented on a standard 12-lead ECG; lateral V5/V6 show reciprocal changes. (Book p425)

questions.sec: Coronary Territories, Dominance & Right Coronary Artery
questions.q: Which named lead group assesses right-ventricular free wall in this chapter?
questions.exp: Right free-wall leads are V3R–V5R. The source separately lists V7–V9 for posterior wall assessment. (Book p425)

questions.sec: Coronary Territories, Dominance & Right Coronary Artery
questions.q: What is the stated origin of the right coronary artery?
questions.exp: The RCA is shown arising in the right AV sulcus. (Book p426)

questions.sec: Coronary Territories, Dominance & Right Coronary Artery
questions.q: An inferior MI is accompanied by sinus bradycardia after proximal RCA occlusion. Which RCA branch mechanism is most directly implicated?
questions.exp: The SA nodal branch section states proximal RCA occlusion can cause sinus bradycardia; bradycardia can also reflect vagal stimulation or nodal ischaemia. (Book p426)

questions.sec: Coronary Territories, Dominance & Right Coronary Artery
questions.q: Atrial arrhythmias after proximal RCA occlusion are linked to compromise of which branch group?
opts: Atrial branches in the right AV sulcus
questions.exp: Atrial branches run in the right atrioventricular sulcus; proximal RCA occlusion is linked to atrial arrhythmias. (Book p426)

questions.sec: Coronary Territories, Dominance & Right Coronary Artery
questions.q: An RCA occlusion proximal to the acute marginal artery is most likely to have which implication?
opts: RVMI is present and prognosis is poorer
questions.exp: Occlusion relation to acute marginal artery: proximal means RVMI always positive and poorer prognosis; distal means RVMI always negative. (Book p426)

questions.sec: Coronary Territories, Dominance & Right Coronary Artery
questions.q: Which structure does the acute marginal artery supply?
questions.exp: The acute marginal artery supplies the RV free wall. (Book p426)

questions.sec: Coronary Territories, Dominance & Right Coronary Artery
questions.q: An IWMI patient is hypotensive, has clear lung fields and elevated JVP. What is the source's immediate management direction?
questions.exp: The page's RVMI triangle is hypotension, clear lung fields and raised JVP, with management IV fluids. (Book p426)

questions.sec: Coronary Territories, Dominance & Right Coronary Artery
questions.q: In a right-dominant circulation, distal RCA occlusion produces which infarct pattern?
questions.exp: RCA occlusion flowchart: right dominant proximal → RVMI+IWMI±PWMI; right dominant distal → IWMI±PWMI. Left-dominant distal RCA causes no MI. (Book p426)

questions.sec: Coronary Territories, Dominance & Right Coronary Artery
questions.q: Which complication group is listed under IWMI?
opts: LBBB with high-grade infra-His block only
SA/AV nodal dysfunction, complete heart block, atrial tachycardia, RVMI and posteromedial papillary-muscle rupture
VT/VF, external rupture and septal rupture only
questions.exp: IWMI list includes SA node/AV node/complete heart block, atrial tachycardia, RVMI, and posteromedial papillary muscle rupture causing secondary MR. (Book p426)

questions.sec: Inferior MI Localisation & Left Coronary Anatomy
questions.q: Inferior ST elevation is greater in lead III than lead II, with ST depression in aVL greater than aVR. Which culprit artery does the source favour?
questions.exp: For RCA: ST↑ in II/III/aVF, reciprocal V1/V5/V6; III > II and ST↓ aVL > aVR. LCx instead has II > III. (Book p427)

questions.sec: Inferior MI Localisation & Left Coronary Anatomy
questions.q: An IWMI ECG has ST depression in V1 discordant to V2–V3. What associated extension does the page indicate?
questions.exp: Proximal RCA: ST depression in V1 discordant to V2/V3 is marked RVMI positive. ‘Wrap around’ indicates RCA supplies all regions. (Book p427)

questions.sec: Inferior MI Localisation & Left Coronary Anatomy
questions.q: Which lead relationship favours LCx occlusion in an inferior/posterior MI pattern?
opts: ST elevation in II greater than III
ST elevation in III greater than II
ST depression in aVL greater than aVR
questions.exp: The LCx note lists IWMI+PWMI and ST elevation in II > III; in left dominance, LCx lateral-wall supply may add LWMI. (Book p427)

questions.sec: Inferior MI Localisation & Left Coronary Anatomy
questions.q: After an inferior MI and PCI, a patient has pulmonary congestion, an LV S3, no murmur, good EF, and a normal/near-normal ECG. Which mechanical diagnosis should still be suspected?
questions.exp: The page identifies papillary muscle rupture → secondary MR in post-IWMI PCI with CCF; it notes LV S3, absent murmur, good EF and normal/near-normal ECG. (Book p427)

questions.sec: Inferior MI Localisation & Left Coronary Anatomy
questions.q: Where does the LAD run according to the left-coronary-circulation diagram?
questions.exp: LCA branches into LCx and LAD; the LAD site is the left anterior interventricular sulcus. (Book p427)

questions.sec: Inferior MI Localisation & Left Coronary Anatomy
questions.q: Which branch–territory association is correctly stated?
opts: D1 supplies high lateral wall and septal branches supply septal wall
D1 supplies posterior wall and S1 supplies lateral wall
questions.exp: LCx/LAD branch map: D1 high lateral wall, S1 septal wall, D2 anterior wall, D3 lateral wall; D=diagonal and S=septal. (Book p427)

questions.sec: Inferior MI Localisation & Left Coronary Anatomy
questions.q: Which lead grouping is designated as high lateral MI territory?
questions.exp: LAD/LCx lead map: anterior V2–V4, lateral V5–V6, high lateral I/aVL, septal V1>>V2, apical V1. (Book p427)

questions.sec: LAD Localisation, Left-Main Occlusion & Complications
questions.q: Which LAD-occlusion location is listed before the first diagonal (D1) branch?
questions.exp: The localisation list proceeds: before D1; between D1 and S1; and below S1 (with branches S1–D2 or D2–D3). (Book p428)

questions.sec: LAD Localisation, Left-Main Occlusion & Complications
questions.q: An anteroseptal high-lateral MI has ST elevation in V2–V4, V1, and I/aVL. Which localisation bundle does the page assign?
opts: LAD above S1 and before D1
questions.exp: For anteroseptal high-lateral MI: V2–V4 elevation indicates LAD, V1 elevation indicates above S1, and I/aVL elevation indicates before D1. (Book p428)

questions.sec: LAD Localisation, Left-Main Occlusion & Complications
questions.q: ST elevation in V2–V4 is present but V1 lacks elevation. What LAD localisation does this support?
questions.exp: The wrap-around section says V2–V4 elevation is above D2; V1 no elevation is below S1; II/V5/V6 elevation identifies wrap-around. (Book p428)

questions.sec: LAD Localisation, Left-Main Occlusion & Complications
questions.q: An anterior infarct has ST elevation in II, V5 and V6 in addition to anterior leads. Which anatomical pattern is represented?
questions.exp: The page explicitly labels II, V5 and V6 elevation as wrap-around phenomenon; course enters posterior interventricular sulcus and anastomoses with PDA. (Book p428)

questions.sec: LAD Localisation, Left-Main Occlusion & Complications
questions.q: An anterolateral MI is anatomically described as which relationship?
opts: S1 before D1 with occlusion between S1 and D1
D1 before S1 with occlusion below S1
questions.exp: The source states anterolateral MI has anatomical S1 before D1 and occlusion between S1 and D1. (Book p428)

questions.sec: LAD Localisation, Left-Main Occlusion & Complications
questions.q: V1 ST elevation with ST depression in I and aVL is shown under which infarct localisation?
questions.exp: The anteroseptal section labels V1 ST elevation as above S1 and I/aVL ST depression as between D1 and S1. (Book p428)

questions.sec: LAD Localisation, Left-Main Occlusion & Complications
questions.q: An ECG shows ST elevation in aVR with ST depression in all other leads. What urgent intervention does the source prescribe?
opts: Immediate PCI for proximal left-coronary/left-main occlusion
questions.exp: Proximal LCA occlusion: aVR ST elevation, all other leads ST depression, 100% mortality if untreated; immediate PCI is specified. (Book p429)

questions.sec: LAD Localisation, Left-Main Occlusion & Complications
questions.q: Which electrical complications are listed for LV involvement in AWMI?
opts: Ventricular tachycardia, ventricular fibrillation and sudden cardiac death
Atrial flutter and sinus bradycardia only
questions.exp: AWMI LV involvement includes VT, VF and sudden cardiac death; mechanical complications include external cardiac rupture and septal rupture, plus infra-Hisian blocks. (Book p429)

questions.sec: LAD Localisation, Left-Main Occlusion & Complications
questions.q: Which conduction abnormality is named among AWMI complications?
questions.exp: The AWMI complication list includes infra-Hisian blocks, in contrast to the nodal problems emphasised in IWMI. (Book p429)

units.title: 1. Coronary Territories, Dominance & Right Coronary Artery
units.sec: Coronary Territories, Dominance & Right Coronary Artery
units.guide:
Coronary circulation is first mapped to infarct territory and heart surface.
Dominance is defined by the PDA, then RCA anatomy predicts ECG and complications.
Proximal-versus-distal logic is retained exactly as in the source.

units.title: 2. Inferior MI Localisation & Left Coronary Anatomy
units.sec: Inferior MI Localisation & Left Coronary Anatomy
units.guide:
Inferior-wall ECG details distinguish RCA and LCx occlusion.
Papillary-muscle rupture is separated from global pump failure.
LCA branches and lead territories are then mapped in anatomical order.

units.title: 3. LAD Localisation, Left-Main Occlusion & Complications
units.guide:
Sequential diagonal and septal branches localise LAD occlusion.
Wrap-around anatomy is tied to lead patterns.
Left-main ECG and lethal LV complications complete the chapter.
